title: Dragon Ball Super Remake Confirms Release Date for Next Major Update
content:
Dragon Ball Super is gearing up for its next major update for its new remake anime coming later this Fall, but only some lucky fans will be able to check it out. Dragon Ball Super is on the cusp of a major comeback as not only is the artist behind the manga offering up new pieces to keep the franchise alive , but the anime franchise is coming back with the first of a new wave of releases later this year. And it’s going to offer an enhanced version of the original TV series.

Dragon Ball Super: Beerus is an enhanced version of the original Dragon Ball Super TV series , and will be offering a new take on the Battle of Gods arc. Currently scheduled for a release later this Fall, there are all sorts of other updates that fans are still hoping to get before its release. It seems that next update is coming soon as the anime has announced it will be hosting a special panel at New York Comic Con 2026 this October. Which will hopefully lead to its premiere.

Dragon Ball Super Announces NYCC 2026 Panel

Dragon Ball Super: Beerus is currently scheduled to make its debut sometime this Fall, but has yet to confirm a release date for its launch as of this time. “Fall” usually means a release in October to air alongside a slate of new releases for the Fall 2026 anime schedule, but that’s not always the case. If there are fewer episodes than a usual cour, then the anime could kick off its run later in the year. That might be the case with this one considering it’s only been confirmed to cover the Battle of Gods and Resurrection F arcs .

Dragon Ball Super: Beerus has yet to confirm how many episodes this remake is going to run for, and the anime might have a new time slot altogether. There have been other new anime releases confirmed for the time slots that Dragon Ball Daima had when it aired, and when Dragon Ball Super first ran on TV, so there could be another shake up when it comes to this release. But this panel will likely reveal exactly when the anime will finally premiere. It’s kind of the final big opportunity to do so before the end of the year.

What’s Next for Dragon Ball Super?

Dragon Ball Super: Beerus is coming out later this Fall, and this NYCC 2026 panel is going to be the final major time that the franchise could update fans. There will be a chance later in year with Jump Festa 2027 scheduled for later this December , but by then hopefully we’ve already seen the remake in action. Anyway, there’s much more to look ahead to with Dragon Ball Super’ s future as there’s a brand new anime now in the works as well to take its story further through the manga and potentially beyond.

Dragon Ball Super: The Galactic Patrol is now in the works, but the anime has yet to confirm a potential release as of the time of this writing . It’s been teased that it might be coming our way 2027 or later, and is going to be adapting the Galactic Patrol Prisoner arc. This is an arc currently exclusive to the manga at this time, so it’s an exciting step forward for the franchise on a whole.

title: Nickelodeon Creator Shoots Down Revival Series Rumors
content:
Earlier this month, a former creator of the classic Nickelodeon revival teased that there were active discussions between the original team and Paramount. With the franchise not confirming any new projects since it returned to the screen in 2017, many animation enthusiasts were excited to see what would come next for the city-dwelling cast of colorful characters. Unfortunately, it appears as though the original statement from writer Joe Purdy wasn’t exactly what it seemed, as the original creator of the NickToon has gone on record to throw some cold water on the idea of Arnold and his crew making a return.

Hey Arnold! writer Joe Purdy recently stated that “we were having conversations,” hinting at the idea that the NickToon might receive a revival at Paramount. In a statement to shoot down the idea, original series creator Craig Bartlett shot down the idea that a revival series was in the works, going so far as to say that Purdy’s comments were ‘taken out of context.’ Specifically, Bartlett shared a new social media post that stated, “Here to tell you that the stories this week about being in talks with Paramount are not true. Joe made some comments that were taken out of context. Sorry, gang, but don’t worry, there’s lots of Arnold stuff to keep me busy all year!”

What’s Next For Arnold?

While Bartlett shot down the idea of a Hey Arnold! returning anytime soon, he has discussed the idea of bringing back the series and what the creative team might do should they return to the Nickelodeon universe. Most recently, Craig took part in an anniversary celebration for the series, discussing where Arnold might go should he hit the screen once again: “Obviously, it has to be something Nickelodeon wants. If we were to make something new for Nickelodeon, I would love to just pick up where we left off. I actually really tried to design Hey Arnold! The Jungle Movie to end not as a cliffhanger. I really wanted it to be resolved, but you know, Helga and Arnold know that they love each other now. So what’s gonna happen?”

If you’re wondering what Bartlett was referring to when mentioning how he was still busy with the franchise in 2026, this year will see a real-world tour , “ The Music of Hey Arnold! Live! ” Not only will musicians Jim Land and the PS118 AllStars be playing tracks from the Nickelodeon series, but Craig Bartlett will also be there to offer new insight into the creation of the NickToon. Beginning in California on October 26th, the tour will travel across the country before coming to an end this December. If you want to revisit the series proper, Hey Arnold! is currently streaming on Paramount+.

title: 10 Years Later, Bleach Just Shocked With Ichigo’s Brand New Bankai With Official Name From Creator
content:
Ten years after the original series came to an end, Bleach is still shocking fans with the debut of a brand new Bankai for Ichigo Kurosaki from the original creator making its debut in the latest episode. Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War is working its way through the final season of its episodes adapting Tite Kubo’s original manga, and the latest episode made one of the most significant changes to the manga’s original events yet with an extension to the fight between Ichigo and Yhwach. And that includes a brand new form.

Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War Episode 5 continues the final fight between Ichigo and Yhwach, and it made a major change to things with the latest episode. While previous changes have extended the events of certain fights or revealed new forms , this latest change has to be the biggest yet as it’s introduced a brand new Bankai form for Ichigo that he never used in the original series. Officially dubbed Blood Chains Ichigo, you can check out Tite Kubo’s official design for the new Bankai below.

Bleach: TYBW Debuts Blood Chains Ichigo Bankai From Tite Kubo

Blood Chains Ichigo is a brand new form that was never seen in Tite Kubo’s original Bleach manga. Around this time in the original depiction of the fight, the manga was quickly heading towards its grand finale. As a true show of power from Yhwach he had interrupted Ichigo before he was able to use his Bankai, but the anime has allowed Ichigo to reach the point where he was able to successfully use this ability and unlock a powerful new form. But it’s still not enough to take on Yhwach’s Almighty power.

Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War has been making all sorts of huge changes to the original version of the manga’s final arc through the first three seasons so far, but we’re about to see even more significant changes now that the anime is heading into its grand finale. With fewer episodes slated for this final season than the others , we’re already at the halfway point of this grand finale and are about to see some major shake ups to everything as a result thanks to how involved Tite Kubo has been with the anime’s production.

How Is Bleach: TYBW Actually Going to End?

It was already exciting to reach this point in Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War as fans have been waiting over ten years for the anime to adapt the manga’s grand finale , but the changes seen with this episode make things even more exciting. The manga notably had a truncated finale that seemed to rush through the final battle, and this is a clear extension to make it last longer. Kubo has been directly involved with all of the changes so far, and that’s most significantly going to be felt for now.

Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War is the best version of the manga’s final arc as been seen through the episodes so far, and it seems to be the most complete version of the story that Kubo has been refining for years at this point. Debuting new forms like this ahead of what could be the end of this very long battle could just be the first in many more surprises to come. Make sure to catch up with it all on Hulu and Hulu on Disney+.

title: Yen Press Reveals 9 New Licenses Including Übel Blatt II, The Gray Exorcist, Seal My Lips With a Kiss Manga
content:
Yen Press announced nine new licenses at its main industry panel at Anime NYC on Saturday, including two light novel series and seven manga series. The company did not give a release window for the new licenses.

The two new light novel licenses include:

Leonardo Nix once dreamed of becoming an alchemist. Instead, he's in a maximum- security prison, languishing in guilt and self-disgust. After all, he admitted to breaking an unspeakable taboo—eating his comrades. Then, not long into his imprisonment, he is suddenly transformed into a hideous monstrosity. He flees the prison as guards sound the alarm, but nowhere is safe for such a terrible beast. And though he doesn't want to hurt anyone, a dark hunger for human flesh stirs within him. When all hope seems lost, he crosses paths with Elena the witch, who offers to find a way to break his curse! Unfortunately, there's a catch: As her familiar, he'll still get blood on his hands...straying even farther from the path of redemption.

Faye Leonheart is a seventeen-year-old sword-fighting prodigy and the heir apparent to the mightiest warrior clan. After three long years, she finally returns from her sword- training pilgrimage...with a magical machine gun in hand?! Promptly disowned by her family with nothing but her beloved firearm for company, this trigger-happy young lady commits herself to studying ancient technology called overgear. After all, who has time for regrets when freedom calls? The world is full of archaic ruins, and Faye is ready to explore them, full-metal style!

The seven new manga licenses include:

“If this comes undone...I don't know what I'll do...”

Kaede's never seen this side of her unassuming STEM coworker, but his words and her position at his mercy start to light a fire in her...!

MangaPlaza is also releasing the manga in English digitally.

Manga UP! Global is also releasing the manga in English digitally.

ANN's coverage of Anime NYC 2026 is sponsored by Yen Press. Whether it's light novels, manga, or manhwa, Yen Press has everything you might want to add to your reading shelves! Visit Booth #1701 or YenPress.com for more information!

title: Ize Press Announces Whale Star, Solo Leveling Releases at Anime NYC
content:
Ize Press announced four new titles at Yen Press ' industry panel at Anime NYC , including the acclaimed webtoon Whale Star: The Gyeongseong Mermaid and several new releases expanding its Solo Leveling lineup.

Written by Yoonhee Na, Whale Star: The Gyeongseong Mermaid is a historical romance set in Korea under Japanese colonial rule in 1926. The story follows Sooah, a young maid who becomes involved with Uihyeon, a wounded independence fighter she discovers while he is fleeing from Japanese authorities. The six-volume series was originally serialized on WEBTOON and has surpassed 13 million readers. It won the 2021 Korea Content Grand Prize Presidential Award and is also receiving a live-action adaptation.

Fans can read the English version of the webtoon on WEBTOON .

Ize Press will also release a Spanish-language edition of Solo Leveling in comic, novel, and audiobook formats. The comic and novel editions will be available in the United States and Canada, while the audiobook have a worldwide release.

The publisher is also adding the Solo Leveling: Ragnarok sequel novel series by Daul . The sequel follows Sooho Sung, the son of original protagonist Jinwoo Sung, as he becomes involved with the world of hunters and monsters. Ize Press started releasing the comic version of Solo Leveling: Ragnarok in print in July.

Fans can read the English version of the web novel on Tapas .

Finally, Ize Press announced Solo Leveling : The Board Game , a cooperative tactical tabletop game for one to four players featuring characters, monsters, and bosses from the series. The company will release both Standard and Ultimate editions, with the latter featuring additional collectibles including a Beru plushie.

Ize Press will reveal release dates, pricing, and additional details for the new titles at a later date.

title: Vampire Hunter D Returns With 2026 US Release
content:
When it comes to slaying vampires, there is one anime character who has been front and center in terms of laying creatures of the night to rest. Even though it’s been decades since we last witnessed D staking some vamps, thanks to Vampire Hunter D: Bloodlust , the swordsman still finds his way back into the public eye. Recently, Dark Horse Comics announced that not only is it bringing D back, but it will be adapting classic stories involving the son of Dracula for North America. While a new anime adaptation has yet to be revealed, these projects might lead us to seeing D back on the screen.

Dark Horse shared that a new comic book series was set to adapt a classic D story in Vampire Hunter D: Fortress of Blood . While not based on any of the previous stories from the novel series or anime films, this four-issue storyline is spawned from a concept from Vampire Hunter D’s creator Hideyuki Kikuchi. Written by author Chris Condon and drawn by artist Filipe Andrade, the series is planning to release its first issue in December of this year. In the story, D struggles with a new vampire lord who is dead set on eradicating humanity and must now attempt to lay siege to an impenetrable fortress. This comic series isn’t the only D-centric series that Dark Horse is releasing.

Vampire Hunter D’s Big Comeback

Alongside this upcoming four-issue series , Dark Horse is also planning to translate Vampire Hunter D: The Rose Princess into English for a North American release. Landing in June 2027, the manga revolves around a female vampire princess who terrorizes a village and claims victims at her discretion. With one villager attempting to save his beloved from a fanged fate, he enlists the aid of D to go on a quest to defeat the evil. The original story was published as a novel in the 1990s, arriving as the ninth major story of the Vampire Hunter D franchise.

On top of the big announcements regarding the return of D , series creator Hideyuki Kikuchi shared his approval for the project and stated, “I am deeply honored to finally see the adaptation of D into an American comic book. I never could have imagined that D, a series born in Japan, would be reborn in the form of an American Comic. I would like to express my gratitude to Dark Horse Comics for making this a reality, and above all, to the people that help make it happen, Michael Gombos , the editor, Judy Khuu, as well as to Filipe Andrade, who created the wonderful illustrations, and Chris Condon, who crafted a superb script tailored for the American comic book format from my original scenario! I hope that this comic will serve as a catalyst for the story of D to spread beyond Japan and the United States, and reach the entire world.”

title: New The Apothecary Diaries Season 3 Trailer Confirms Crunchyroll Release Date – Watch
content:
The Apothecary Diaries is making a massive return later this Fall with more of the anime than ever, and a new trailer from Crunchyroll is showing off Season 3 ahead of its October release date. The anime adaptation for Hyūganatsu’s The Apothecary Diaries has been an absolute runaway success since it made its debut, and has quickly returned for even more episodes. But it’s getting ready for its biggest season yet with a third batch of episodes coming later this Fall, and a new feature film coming to theaters too .

The Apothecary Diaries Season 3 is making its return to Crunchyroll later this October as part of their jam packed Fall 2026 slate of exclusives , and it’s going to be offering the first cour of its episodes before it returns in 2027. This third season is kicking off a disastrous new arc for Maomao and the others as a major locust problem is ushering in a famine that could lead to the destruction of everything. Check it all out in action below.

When Does The Apothecary Diaries Season 3 Come Out?

The Apothecary Diaries Season 3 will be making its debut on October 2nd , and it will be exclusively streaming with Crunchyroll as part of their Fall 2026 schedule. The anime will then be taking a break in the Winter months next year before then returning for its second cour of episodes sometime in April 2027 as part of the Spring 2027 schedule. This new trailer also reveals some big updates about the new additions to the cast along with the first tease of the new season’s opening theme, “Kumo o Nukekazashimo e Watashidake” as performed by yorushika.

New additions to the cast for The Apothecary Diaries Season 3 include Reina Ueda as Bai Niangniang, who is teased to play a big role in the coming arc. But while this seems to be a mystery that Maomao may not be able to solve, it’s something that is going to be much bigger than anything that she has ever faced before. But like the other seasons before it, fans are likely going to love following Maomao as she digs further into this newest mystery.

What’s Next for The Apothecary Diaries?

This isn’t going to be all for the franchise, however, as The Apothecary Diaries also has a new feature film coming to theaters later this year as well. title: One Piece Drops New Look Trailer for Netflix LEGO Special – Watch Now
content:
One Piece is coming back to Netflix later this Fall with an official LEGO makeover, and now fans have gotten a new look at what to expect with a new trailer showing it all off. One Piece has been a massive hit with Netflix ever since it debuted its official live-action series adaptation , and that success has resulted in two seasons so far. With a third season of the live-action series in the works, there’s even more from the franchise on the way as Netflix has even more projects coming down the pipeline.

LEGO ONE PIECE is a new special coming to Netflix this September , and it’s going to be offering a fun new reimagining of the live-action series’ events told through a fun LEGO style. Seeing Usopp recounting the adventures of the Straw Hat pirates over the course of the first two seasons to a Chopper that has no idea how much Usopp is lying about it all, it’s definitely going to be a great way to get hyped for that coming season. You can check it out in action below.

When Does LEGO One Piece Special Come Out on Netflix?

LEGO One Piece is teased to be a two part special making its debut with Netflix on September 29th , and it will be retelling the events of the first two seasons through Usopp’s own unique vision. The trailer also finds a way to tie it back into the canon of the live-action series through this too as it does make a lot of sense that Usopp would be catching Tony Tony Chopper up on everything that happened before he joined the crew. And this gives the opportunity for the live-action crew to lean more into the comedy of it al.

The live-action One Piece cast will be reprising their roles for the new LEGO specia too with Iñaki Godoy as Monkey D. Luffy, Mackenyu as Roronoa Zoro, Emily Rudd as Nami, Jacob Romero as Usopp, Taz Skylar as Sanji, Charithra Chandran as Miss Wednesday, and Mikaela Hoover as Tony Tony Chopper all confirmed. And after fans get more One Piece through this LEGO special later this Fall, there is going to be much more of the franchise coming to Netflix in 2027 with both anime and live-action releases planned.

What’s New for One Piece on Netflix in 2027?

One Piece has been such a hit with Netflix that the streaming service has been in the works on multiple releases for the franchise. This LEGO special is only one cool new release as One Piece: The Battle of Alabasta ( the official name of the live-action series’ third season ) is currently scheduled to come to the platform sometime in 2027. A release date has yet to be confirmed as of this time, but it’s going to feature lots of new faces in Luffy’s biggest battle yet.

That’s not all that’s on the way either as One Piece also has an exclusive anime now in the works too. The One Piece is a brand new remake anime series scheduled to release with Netflix in February 2027 , and will be adapting Eiichiro Oda’s original manga from the very beginning. Brought to life by WIT Studio, it’s going to kick off a huge new year for the franchise on Netflix.

title: BLEACH: Thousand-Year Blood War Reveals Ichigo's New Blood Chain Bankai Form in Visual and Video
content:
BLEACH: Thousand-Year Blood War (TYBW) Part 4 revealed a new visual and video to show Ichigo’s new “blood chain” form. The anime returned with the fourth and final cour, subtitled The Calamity , on July 25. It is set to run for 10 episodes. In last week’s episode, Zaraki and Toshiro revealed their Bankai abilities, with Yuki Kaji joining the voice cast as the older version of Toshiro.

You can watch the clip from the latest episode below.

ALSO READ: BLEACH JET Artbook and Ryogo Narita’s School Life Novel Return, Fan Vote and 2027 Exhibition Announced

A special visual for BLEACH THE STORIES was also revealed, also featuring Ichigo’s new form.

Created by Tite Kubo, BLEACH was serialized in Weekly Shonen Jump from 2001 to 2016 and concluded with 74 volumes. The manga has exceeded 130 million copies in circulation worldwide, making it one of the best-selling manga series of all time.

The original anime adaptation aired from 2004 to 2012 and received four theatrical films. The franchise returned in 2022 with BLEACH: Thousand-Year Blood War , adapting the manga’s final arc. Its final part (Part 4) is set to release in July. Tite Kubo has confirmed it will include even more original material than the previous parts , expanding the manga’s final battles.

On a related note, BLEACH: Mirrors High revealed its protagonists in a new trailer, with the game featuring original character designs by Tite Kubo.

title: 12 Years Ago, Netflix’s Most Depressing Animated Series Debuted
content:
Netflix has created its fair share of original programming to help prove it’s become a premier spot for streaming, with the animation world being no exception. While the streaming service has created heart-pounding action series like Devil May Cry and Castlevania , it also created plenty of comedies, including Big Mouth and Inside Job . Amongst the many animated series Netflix has created in its history, only one can be universally thought of as the most “depressing” entry in the platform’s library. Twelve years ago, fans were introduced to a former television star whose journey could sometimes be tough to watch.

In 2014, Bojack Horseman debuted on Netflix, following the titular character as he struggled with his life now that his fame had faded. While Bojack never needed to worry much about money, thanks to being the star of a 90’s sitcom titled “Horsin’ Around,” he had plenty of other things to worry about. Bojack himself was never the best of people, constantly finding himself running afoul of his friends while never quite finding the acceptance he was looking for. Throughout the six seasons of the show, Bojack messes up quite a bit, losing friends and making enemies, but eventually finds the happiest ending that someone like himself could find. So why did Bojack Horseman end after seventy-six episodes?

Bojack Horseman’s Legacy

Despite having quite the lengthy run on Netflix, Bojack’s story would end in 2020, and it wasn’t the creators’ decision. Series creator Raphael Bob-Waksberg has gone on record that the streaming service ultimately decided to end Bojack Horseman with season six, despite the fact that the animator had ideas for “several more years” of the animated series. Even though Bojack’s depressing story would end prematurely, Bob-Waksberg was still happy with the run it ultimately had, noting in previous interviews that many Netflix shows would never have the chance to run for six seasons.

As for the appeal of Bojack Horseman , the anthropomorphic universe saw Bojack messing up his life time and time again, routinely costing him friends and family as a result. While Horseman wouldn’t try to be malicious over the course of six seasons, many found themselves caught up in his addictive personality. Even though the animated series ended prematurely, it did end in a place that felt organic for the titular character.

While Bojack isn’t likely to return, this hasn’t stopped the animated show’s creator from exploring new territory. In 2025, Bob-Waksberg created a new series titled Long Story Short , which followed a human family as viewers explored their past, present, and future. This animated series was confirmed for a second season following its premiere season; Netflix has yet to confirm when the tear-jerker will make its grand return.
